records.headline: Sir Patrick Stewart, Star Trek and X-Men actor, dies at 86
records.text: Patrick Stewart, the British actor best known for playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, died Wednesday at 86 after a brief illness. Born in Yorkshire in 1940, he began his career with Britain's Royal Shakespeare Company and National Theatre before moving to Hollywood. He won two Olivier awards for stage work and a Grammy for narration, and was nominated for four Emmys.

storyboard.concept: A career arc traced through distinct professional stages, from foundational stage work through major screen roles to recognition across multiple media formats

beats.action: A captain's chair (iconic silhouette, not branded) materializes at center. The figure sits. A command console outline appears before the chair. Stars suggest the setting without photorealism.

beats.evidence: Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films
beats.action: A second distinct chair appears stage right (different design, no wheelchair imagery). The figure rises from the captain's chair and moves toward this new chair, illustrating transition between roles. Both chairs remain visible.

beats.evidence: He won two Olivier awards for stage work and a Grammy for narration, and was nominated for four Emmys
beats.action: Abstract award forms (geometric shapes representing trophies/recognitions—not realistic statuettes) emerge above both the stage area and the chairs. records.headline: Binance freezes billions after suspected $6.3 billion security breach
records.text: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer allowed hackers to steal an estimated $6.3 billion. Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze $1.57 billion and $800 million respectively in linked assets. Bitcoin dropped more than 3% to a six-week low, and Coinbase Global shares fell 4.8%, but analysts said the market appeared confident Binance had enough financial resources to cover user losses.

Simultaneously, a large numerical value (6.3B) begins flowing out of the device as a stream of particles/data moving rightward off-screen. This represents the theft without depicting violence.

beats.evidence: Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze $1.57 billion and $800 million respectively in linked assets
beats.action: Frame 2: Two separate containers or vaults appear on-screen (one labeled conceptually for Tether, one for Circle). A pause or lock symbol appears over each. Dollar amounts are shown entering these vaults and stopping mid-flow. The visual shows containment/halting of asset movement, not destruction.

beats.evidence: Bitcoin dropped more than 3% to a six-week low
beats.action: Frame 3: A line chart or price indicator shows a downward slope. A small Bitcoin symbol descends along this line. A timeline marker indicates 'six-week' span in conceptual terms (not literal calendar). The decline is visible but moderate, not catastrophic.

beats.evidence: Coinbase Global shares fell 4.8%
beats.action: Frame 4: A stock price indicator or bar shows a slight downward movement labeled with 4.8%. This appears adjacent to but separate from the Bitcoin chart, emphasizing this is a stock market reaction, not cryptocurrency price movement.

beats.evidence: analysts said the market appeared confident Binance had enough financial resources to cover user losses
beats.action: Frame 5: The outflowing 6.3B stream from Frame 1 is now shown being intercepted or caught by a conceptual barrier/shield labeled as 'reserves' or shown as a stabilizing force. Market stability symbols (upward trending, balanced scale) appear. The visual suggests confidence in containment/recovery without claiming certainty.

records.headline: Spain observes three-day mourning period as at least 69 die in high-speed train collision
records.text: A high-speed train from Renfe collided with a stationary train from Iryo near Urda on Wednesday morning, killing at least 69 people. The crash occurred on the same route where 46 people died ten months earlier. This was Europe's deadliest train accident since 2013.

records.headline: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde steps down nine months early
records.text: Christine Lagarde announced she is stepping down as European Central Bank president nine months early, effective February 2027, to gain freedom to speak publicly on broader issues. She said ECB rules of neutrality prevented her from engaging in important debates about economic matters and truth. Her early departure triggers a succession race to lead the eurozone's central bank during a period of weak growth and inflation of 3.8 percent.

records.headline: Israeli election produces no clear winner as Arab parties make historic gains
records.text: Israel's election produced no clear winner as Prime Minister Netanyahu's coalition and the opposition both fell short of the 61 seats needed to govern. Arab-led parties made historic gains, winning 19 seats, prompting Netanyahu to claim foreign interference; Qatar denied the accusations and election officials found no evidence of systematic violations. President Herzog will consult with party leaders and choose a candidate to attempt forming a government.

records.headline: US intelligence surveilled Chinese executive believed targeting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
records.text: US intelligence agencies surveilled Alice Huang, a Chinese executive at Singapore data center firm Megaspeed, after concluding she was a Chinese intelligence asset targeting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. An Nvidia spokesperson denied anything improper, saying executive meetings with customers are routine business. Trump was briefed on the matter a year ago but took no action, and Jensen Huang was not given a defensive briefing that would typically alert him to the surveillance.

The line of focus is now bidirectional: from the Megaspeed node toward the Nvidia node, illustrating the reported targeting relationship.

records.headline: Australian court orders Erin Patterson never be released from prison for mushroom poisonings
records.text: Victoria's Court of Appeal ordered Erin Patterson to never be released from prison for poisoning her estranged husband's family members with death cap mushrooms at a lunch she hosted in July 2023. The court found the crimes involved careful planning and calculated deception, and that a 33-year non-parole term failed to reflect the calculated criminality. Patterson can apply to Australia's High Court for a final appeal.

records.headline: Hong Kong leader apologises for government failures in residential fire that killed 168 people
records.text: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee apologised for government failures that contributed to a November 2025 fire at Wang Fuk Court housing complex that killed 168 people. An independent investigation found decades of regulatory failure and "lax enforcement" by four government departments. Housing Secretary Winnie Ho resigned, and authorities charged seven individuals and two companies with offences including manslaughter, though some victims' families said political accountability fell short.

records.headline: Korean films 'Journey There' and 'Nowhere to Lay My Eyes' secure international distribution deals
records.text: Seoul-based sales company Finecut announced international distribution deals for 'Journey There,' starring Netflix actor Justin H. Min, and Hong Sangsoo's 'Nowhere to Lay My Eyes,' which won three awards at the Locarno Film Festival. 'Journey There' sold to distributors in Japan, Taiwan, Israel and Mongolia, while 'Nowhere to Lay My Eyes' added deals in France, Japan, Argentina and Portugal following earlier sales across North America, Europe and Asia.

records.headline: Russian drone strike on Ukrainian train station kills at least 14 people
records.text: A Russian jet-powered drone struck a crowded platform at Dnipro's main railway station Thursday, killing at least 14 people and wounding at least 14 others including an 11-year-old. Separate Russian attacks killed two teenage girls in Chernihiv and three civilians in Kremenchuk. The strikes continued despite a localised ceasefire in the southern city of Oleshky credited by both sides to US first lady Melania Trump's involvement.

The figures represent gathered people; the drone is a simple angular form, not a photographic reconstruction.

beats.action: The platform scene transforms: figures separate into two groups—one group dims/fragments to represent the 14 killed; another group shows disruption with emphasis on one smaller figure (representing the 11-year-old). Numbers appear as text labels only: '14 killed' and '14 wounded' positioned near respective groups. No literal injury depiction.

beats.evidence: Separate Russian attacks killed two teenage girls in Chernihiv and three civilians in Kremenchuk
beats.action: The view pulls back to show the railway station as one point on a simplified regional map. Two additional impact zones appear simultaneously at labeled positions (Chernihiv and Kremenchuk) with smaller geometric disruptions, each paired with numbers: '2' and '3'. This conveys simultaneity of separate strikes without geographic accuracy.

beats.action: A fourth position (Oleshky) appears on the map with a distinct visual state—a contained or separated zone marked differently (e.g., bordered, or with a pause indicator)—to show the reported ceasefire status. records.headline: Canadian Prime Minister and EU Commission president announce alliance against economic coercion
records.text: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced plans for Canada to become the bloc's first "associate member" and form a broader "Alliance for the Future" with other like-minded countries. They warned that economic relationships were increasingly being weaponised as tools of pressure. Trump has suggested the arrangement could be considered hostile and threatened retaliation, though a Canadian official said the closer relationship reflected longstanding shared interests.

records.headline: China expels record 33 members from Communist Party amid intensified purges under Xi
records.text: China expelled a record 33 members from the Communist Party at its fifth plenum this week, amid intensified purges under Xi Jinping. Only 279 of 376 Central Committee members originally named in 2022 attended the gathering, the highest number of absences in modern Chinese history. Xi has removed so many high-ranking officials—51 in his current term alone—that observers worry there are few suitable candidates to fill vacancies ahead of the party congress expected in late 2027.
